newsitem.title: INDIA: India gets Pakistan proposal for electricity sales.
newsitem.headline: India gets Pakistan proposal for electricity sales.

text.p: India has received a proposal from Pakistan for the sale of electricity, Indian Power Minister Y.K. Alagh said in Parliament on Thursday.

A government statement quoted Alagh as saying several World Bank-funded power projects were under implementation in Pakistan, and with the last of these -- the 1300 megawatt Hub River project -- becoming operational, Pakistan would have surplus power.

The statement quoted Alagh as saying technical information was being exchanged, including details concerning the quantity, transport and cost of the electricity as well as the compatibility of the power systems of the two countries.
India and Pakistan first discussed the sale of surplus power last May when prime ministers of both countries met at a regional summit in the Maldives.
India has stated it could buy up to 3,000 megawatts of power from Pakistan by 1998/99 (April-March).
Apart from purchase of power from Pakistan, India is considering similar arrangements with its neighbours, Bangladesh and Nepal.
During the Eigth Plan (1992-97) India could only create fresh capacity for 17,700 megawatts against a targeted 30,538 megawatts. The shortfall is attributed mainly to flagging investment.

Two years ago, the government estimated India needed nearly $80 billion to overcome supply gaps. With the country aiming for a sustained seven percent growth during the Ninth Plan (1997-2002), demand for power is soaring.
